title: Health and the body
goal: Describe being ill at a clinic or hospital — where the wrong word costs the most, and where *pening*, *pusing* and *punggung* really need to be kept apart.
bekal: naming body parts and kinds of pain with Malay words
talking to a doctor and reading medicine instructions
knowing Malaysian hospital and emergency terms

dialogs.title: Dialogue — At the health clinic
dialogs.intro: Sarah has had a fever for two days and finally goes to the health clinic near campus. The nurse calls her in.

lines.speaker: Doktor:
lines.id: Please sit down. What seems to be the problem?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Saya rasa tak sihat, doktor. Demam dua hari dah.
lines.id: I don't feel well, doctor. I've had a fever for two days.
lines.literal: I feel not healthy, doctor. fever two day already.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.id: Yes. A dry cough and a blocked nose.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.id: A little dizzy, especially when I get up.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Tekak sakit sangat bila telan. Badan pun sakit-sakit.
lines.id: My throat really hurts when I swallow. My whole body aches too.
lines.literal: throat sore very when swallow. body also sore-sore.

lines.speaker: Doktor:
lines.text: Saya periksa suhu dulu. Buka mulut, kata 'aaa'.
lines.id: Let me check your temperature first. Open your mouth, say 'aaah'.
lines.literal: I check temperature first. open mouth, say 'aaa'.

lines.speaker: Doktor:
lines.text: Tiga puluh lapan koma lima. Tekak awak merah. Jangkitan virus biasa.
lines.id: Thirty-eight point five. Your throat is red. A common viral infection.
lines.literal: three ten eight comma five. throat you red. infection virus common.

lines.speaker: Doktor:
lines.text: Tak perlu. Saya bagi ubat demam dan ubat batuk. Minum air banyak.
lines.id: No need. I'll give you fever medicine and cough medicine. Drink plenty of water.
lines.literal: not need. I give medicine fever and medicine cough. drink water much.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Boleh dapat sijil sakit? Saya kena hantar kat pejabat.
lines.id: Can I get a medical certificate? I have to hand it in at the office.
lines.literal: can get certificate sick? I must send at office.

lines.speaker: Doktor:
lines.text: Boleh. Dua hari rehat. Kalau tak baik juga, datang balik.
lines.id: Yes. Two days' rest. If you don't get better, come back.
lines.literal: can. two day rest. if not good also, come back.

notes: ⚠️ **Pening, not pusing.** This is the most important clinical word in the module. In Malay, **pening** = headache, dizzy, while **pusing** = to spin, go round. Say *saya pusing* to a Malaysian doctor and you'll be asked "go round where?" Say **pening kepala**. (Indonesian uses *pusing* for dizzy — a classic mix-up.)
**Selesema** = a cold, mild flu. It's probably the first word you won't recognize at the clinic.
**Tekak** = throat. *Sakit tekak* (sore throat) is the most common complaint at Malaysian clinics.

**Ubat** = medicine — note the *u*. The whole word family follows: *ubat demam* (fever medicine), *ubat batuk* (cough medicine), *ubat gigi* (⚠️ toothpaste!), *perubatan* (medical treatment), *kedai ubat* (pharmacy, drugstore).

grammars.title: Parts of the body
body: Most of these you just need to learn. The tricky ones are marked — and two of them could have you pointing at the wrong place in front of the doctor.
after: ⚠️ **Belakang** = back, and **punggung** = bottom. You met this in unit 3, but the clinic is where it really matters. *Sakit belakang* = backache. Say *sakit punggung* and the doctor will examine a completely different part. (In Indonesian, *punggung* means back — hence the confusion.)
⚠️ **Buah pinggang** = kidney, literally "fruit of the waist". You'll see it on every Malaysian health document.

head: Malay
English
rows: I have a headache. / I feel dizzy.
I'm hurt / I have a cut.

blocks.text: Four words worth learning by heart: **cirit-birit** (diarrhea), **loya** (nausea), **terseliuh** (sprained), and **alah** (allergic — not to be confused with the exclamation *alah!*, roughly "oh, come on"). For allergy people also say *alahan* or simply *alergi*.
**Tak lalu makan** = to have no appetite. *Lalu* here means "to feel like (eating)", a use found only in this phrase.

blocks.title: Questions the doctor will ask
items: **Apa masalahnya?** — What seems to be the problem?
**Dah berapa lama?** — How long has it been?
**Sakit macam mana? Berdenyut ke, pedih ke?** — What kind of pain? Throbbing or stinging?
**Ada alah pada ubat tak?** — Any drug allergies?
**Ada makan ubat lain?** — Are you taking any other medicine?

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Pembedahan** = surgery. In Malay *operasi* is used more for police or military operations. If the doctor says *awak kena pembedahan*, you need an operation.
**Wad** (from *ward*) = hospital ward. *Masuk wad* = to be admitted to hospital.

head: On the label
Meaning
rows: don't drive after taking the medicine
keep out of reach of children

blocks.title: Emergencies — learn these by heart
items: **Ada kemalangan.** — There's been an accident. (⚠️ *kemalangan* = accident)
**Hospital paling dekat kat mana?** — Where's the nearest hospital?
**Saya perlu doktor sekarang.** — I need a doctor now.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Kemalangan** means **accident** — not general misfortune. *Kemalangan jalan raya* = road accident. It's in the news every day.

items: I have a cold and a cough.
I feel nauseous and I have diarrhea.
I haven't felt well for two days.
Can I get a medical certificate?
